title: The Midnight Veil Anew
premise: When the crown of Veylmark announces a kingdom-wide hunt for magic-bearers, Juniper Reyes—once sworn to the silent god Veil and now a charm-seller scraping by—learns the purge is being driven by the Hollow King: a thing that wears the monarch's body and feeds on the gift itself. Forced out of hiding, Juniper gathers a found family of outlaws—a disgraced inquisitor, a boy whose magic is a curse, and the true heir hidden in a workhouse—and journeys to the capital to unbind the king before the Hollow King's long winter seals the land in permanent dark. At the throne, Juniper must sacrifice her last tether to her silent god to tear the crown-thing loose, discovering Veil's silence was the price of keeping it imprisoned. In the end, the true heir takes a broken throne, magic is decriminalized, and Juniper, mortal and unsworn for the first time, chooses to stay with her found family rather than vanish again.
about_author: Juniper Vasquez is a former night-market vendor who writes fantasy about people the law forgot, drawing on years of living in border cities where survival meant keeping your gifts quiet. She lives with three cats and a stubborn belief that family is something you build, not something you're given.

chapters.title: Charms for the Quiet
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. In the outlawed-magic city of Greyhollow, Juniper sells harmless charms and hides her true gift, mourning her silent god. When a customer is dragged away by crown hunters mid-purchase, the emotional beat is the fragile safety of invisibility shattering. She realizes the purge has reached her door.

chapters.title: The Proclamation on Every Wall
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The crown decrees all gift-bearers must register or die; her neighbor and fellow hidden mage is taken in the night. Juniper burns her ledger of clients, torn between fleeing and fighting. Emotional beat: guilt—she sold them the charms that marked them.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor Who Fell
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Disgraced inquisitor Sera Vane refuses to torture a child with the gift and is branded a traitor. She escapes the order that raised her, carrying stolen documents about the 'Hollowing'—the king's strange illness. Emotional beat: the vertigo of losing the only family she knew.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Night Market
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Sera finds Juniper, offering documents in exchange for a warding charm only a sworn mage can make. Juniper refuses—until Sera reveals the king himself is the source of the purge. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance between a hunted mage and a hunter.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Burned Rain
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam, a workhouse orphan whose uncontrolled magic boils water and scorches skin, is betrayed by the matron to hunters for coin. He flees through Greyhollow's rooftops and stumbles into Juniper's cellar. Emotional beat: terror becoming the first flicker of trust.

chapters.title: What the Veil Demanded
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, with flashbacks. Juniper recounts her swearing to Veil fifteen years ago and the god's sudden silence—the day the king 'fell ill.' She realizes the two events coincide. Emotional beat: grief curdling into purpose; her faith was stolen, not abandoned.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Greyhollow
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The trio flees the city through sewers and checkpoint bribes; Sera kills a former colleague to save Tam and breaks completely. Juniper, who swore never to take another life, shields them with raw magic, burning her cover forever. Emotional beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Chapel of the Silent God
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. They shelter in a ruined Veil-chapel where Sera confesses she signed the order that destroyed Juniper's old circle years ago. Juniper nearly abandons her; Tam forces them to speak honestly. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a choice, not a feeling.

chapters.title: Winter Comes Early
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The Hollow King's winter descends out of season—crops blacken, rivers freeze, and refugees crowd the roads claiming the king's shadow walks at night. Juniper's magic flickers as the land's gift is drained. Emotional beat: dread; the stakes are no longer personal but civilizational.

chapters.title: The Heir in the Workhouse
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera's stolen documents reveal a true heir, smuggled into Greyhollow's workhouses fifteen years ago. They race back to find her before the hunters do—and discover she is Wren, Tam's only friend. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as responsibility.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, a quiet girl who never knew she was royal, refuses the claim—she watched 'important people' decide everyone's fate her whole life. Juniper doesn't argue; she just shows her the frozen fields. Emotional beat: a girl choosing to matter.

chapters.title: The Hollow King's Hunters
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Elite hunters corner the group at a river crossing. Tam, terrified of his own gift, unleashes it fully for the first time—boiling the river, scarring himself. Sera is gravely wounded shielding him. Emotional beat: power and cost arriving together.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Sera's fever won't break without magic Juniper no longer trusts herself to wield. Juniper prays to silent Veil and, for the first time in fifteen years, hears an answer—a single word: 'Come.' Emotional beat: the return of faith, complicated and terrifying.

chapters.title: The God Who Went Quiet
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Following Veil's pull, Juniper communes at a mountain shrine and learns the truth: Veil bound itself into the royal crown generations ago as a seal, and the seal is failing—the Hollow King is what leaks through. Veil went silent to hold the door. Emotional beat: awe and horror; her god was never gone, only drowning.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Sera's POV, convalescent. Sera reveals the inquisition's deepest file: the 'king's illness' rituals are the Hollow King feeding, and the purge exists to harvest gift-bearers as fuel. The group understands the deadline—by midwinter solstice, the seal fails entirely. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the enemy is the throne itself.

chapters.title: The City of Frozen Bells
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The four infiltrate the capital, where bells are frozen mid-ring and citizens move like sleepwalkers under the Hollow King's winter. Wren sees her father's city and grieves a home she never had. Emotional beat: sorrow sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The King in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Reaching the king's chamber, they find the monarch still half-alive inside his own body, begging through cracked lips for release. The Hollow King speaks through him, offering Juniper her god's freedom if she walks away. Emotional beat: temptation made flesh.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. On the solstice night, Juniper begins the unbinding while Sera and Wren hold back the Hollow King's wraith-guard and Tam burns a path. To free Veil, Juniper must surrender her own sworn bond—her magic, her identity, her protection. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the climax's hinge.

chapters.title: The Door in the Dark
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, inside the binding. Stripped of her gift, Juniper walks the collapsing seal alongside Veil itself and pushes the Hollow King back through the door, holding it with her bare human hands while Veil re-knots the lock. Emotional beat: a mortal doing what gods could not—refusing to let go.

chapters.title: After the Long Winter
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The winter breaks; the king dies human and mourned. Wren is crowned in a thawing city and decrees the gift lawful. Sera, pardoned but changed, chooses exile from the new order to guard the seal-shrine. Emotional beat: bittersweet dawn; victory with scars.

chapters.title: The Charm Shop on Lantern Row
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Months later, Juniper—magicless, unsworn—opens a small shop selling honest charms that work by craft, not gift. Tam apprentices with her; Wren visits as a friend, not a queen. Emotional beat: quiet joy; the found family gathered under one roof.

chapters.title: The Veil, Anew
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. On the first anniversary of the thaw, Veil speaks to Juniper once more—not as a sworn servant this time, but as an equal, offering her the choice of the bond again. Juniper declines, and the god, for the first time, says thank you. Emotional beat: peace; she was never the god's, and now she is her own.
